root_cause: The Escape key handling depended exclusively on the native cancel event, which in certain circumstances (e.g., after repeated activations) failed to preventDefault, allowing the dialog to close despite keyboard: false.
repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener for Escape on the dialog element that preventsDefault and replicates the cancel‑listener logic for both modal and non‑modal dialogs, ensuring Escape never dismisses the dialog when keyboard: false.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will no longer close the dialog when opened with keyboard: false, allowing users to dismiss only via explicit actions (Cancel or Send) and satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard accessibility.
functional_risks: Duplicate handling of Escape if both cancel and keydown listeners execute, but hide() is idempotent.
Extra backdrop transitions may occur when keyboard: false, but they are harmless.
Ensure no interference with other components that rely on Escape keydown.
verification_requirements: Press Escape any number of times while the dialog is open with keyboard: false; the dialog must remain open and focus must stay inside the dialog.
Press Escape while the dialog is open with keyboard: true; the dialog must close.
Verify that activating the Cancel or Send buttons still works as expected.
Confirm that focus trapping and modal behavior are unaffected.
